From 4c7a94286ef7ac7301d633f17519fb1bb89d7550 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Ramesh Babu B <ramesh.babu.b@intel.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2021 21:12:41 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] net: stmmac: Clear receive all(RA) bit when promiscuous mode
 is off

In promiscuous mode Receive All bit is set in GMAC packet filter register,
but outside promiscuous mode Receive All bit is not cleared,
which resulted in all network packets are received when toggle (ON/OFF)
the promiscuous mode.

Fixes: e0f9956a3862 ("net: stmmac: Add option for VLAN filter fail queue enable")
Signed-off-by: Ramesh Babu B <ramesh.babu.b@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_core.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_core.c
index 95864f014ffa..f35c03c9f91e 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_core.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/stmicro/stmmac/dwmac4_core.c
@@ -642,6 +642,7 @@ static void dwmac4_set_filter(struct mac_device_info *hw,
 	value &= ~GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_PCF;
 	value &= ~GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_PM;
 	value &= ~GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_PR;
+	value &= ~GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_RA;
 	if (dev->flags & IFF_PROMISC) {
 		/* VLAN Tag Filter Fail Packets Queuing */
 		if (hw->vlan_fail_q_en) {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `dwmac4_core.c`**
   - A new line was added to the `dwmac4_set_filter` function to clear the Receive All (RA) bit in the GMAC packet filter register. The specific line added is:
     ```c
     value &= ~GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_RA;
     ```
   - This modification ensures that when promiscuous mode is turned off, the RA bit is cleared, preventing the device from receiving all network packets.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `dwmac4_core.c` directly addresses a bug related to the handling of the promiscuous mode in the network driver. By clearing the RA bit when promiscuous mode is not active, the patch resolves the issue where all network packets were still being received after toggling the promiscuous mode off. This change is a corrective measure to ensure proper filtering behavior in the network device, thereby enhancing its functionality and performance.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
value &= ~GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_RA;
```
```c
value = GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_PR | GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_RA;
```
```c
if (dev->flags & IFF_PROMISC) {
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when promiscuous mode is toggled off, the Receive All (RA) bit in the GMAC packet filter register is not cleared. The first statement shows that the RA bit is intended to be cleared, but it is not being executed when promiscuous mode is disabled. The second statement indicates that the RA bit is set when promiscuous mode is enabled, but it remains set when the mode is turned off, leading to the device continuing to receive all packets. The third statement checks if promiscuous mode is active, which is where the RA bit should be managed, but the logic fails to clear it when exiting promiscuous mode.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
value &= ~GMAC_PACKET_FILTER_RA;
```
```c
writel(value, ioaddr + GMAC_PACKET_FILTER);
```
Reason:
The first statement explicitly clears the RA bit from the packet filter register when promiscuous mode is turned off. The second statement writes the updated value back to the GMAC packet filter register, ensuring that the RA bit is correctly set or cleared based on the current mode. This fix ensures that the device does not continue to receive all packets when promiscuous mode is disabled, thus restoring the intended packet filtering behavior.
